ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r1.claim: The command to go is repeated after verses of reassurance: Moses and Aaron are now both sent to Pharaoh because God made Aaron a messenger at Moses' request.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r1.anchor: Aaron (sws) was also included in it because he was also made a messenger at Moses’ request

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r2.claim: Remembering God means prayer and preaching; prayer draws strength from God, the source of true preaching, while a weakened or severed connection drains the mission or turns it into Satan's tool.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r2.anchor: Every task of a prophet constitutes God’s remembrance

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r1.claim: Al-wany means slackening or becoming languid; the verb is intransitive and, when made transitive, takes min or fī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r1.anchor: الوني: الفتور، يقال: وني يني وهو فعل لازم، وإذا عدي فبعن وبفي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r2.speaker: بعض البغداديين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r2.claim: Some Baghdadi grammarians claim wanā can also be a defective verb like mā zāla; Ibn Mālik adopted their view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r2.anchor: وزعم بعض البغداديين أنه يأتي فعلا ناقصا من أخوات ما زال وبمعناها، واختاره ابن مالك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r3.claim: A poetic line is cited to illustrate the defective-verb usage of wanā, describing a lover's trait as persisting as long as he exists.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r3.anchor: وأنشد: لا يني الخب شيمة الحب ... ما دام فلا تحسبنه ذا ارعواء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r4.claim: They also say imraʾah anāh for a woman slow to rise; its hamza replaces wāw without a regular pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p334/r4.anchor: وقالوا: امرأة أنآة أي فاترة عن النهوض، أبدلوا من واوها همزة على غير قياس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r1.claim: ولا تنيا means do not grow weak or fall short; it may also mean do not forget God, who remains aware of them wherever they go.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r1.anchor: ولا تنيا أي لا تضعفا ولا تقصرا. وقيل: تنسياني ولا أزال منكما على ذكر حيثما تقلبتما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r2.claim: The remembrance can mean conveying the message, since remembrance covers all worship and conveying revelation is its greatest form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالذكر تبليغ الرسالة فإن الذكر يقع على سائر العبادات، وتبليغ الرسالة من أجلها وأعظمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r3.speaker: ابن وثاب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r3.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads تنيا with kasra on tāʾ by vowel assimilation to the following nūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب: ولا تنيا بكسر التاء إتباعا لحركة النون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r4.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's codex reads ولا تهنا, meaning do not soften or relax, from the words hayyin and layyin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r4.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله ولا تهنا أي ولا تلنا من قولهم هين لين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.claim: Ab and akh do not change in annexation even when used as personal names; naming does not alter أبوك and أخوك.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.anchor: أب وأخ ونحوهما تقول هذا أبوك وأخوك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.claim: When the proper name is فم, annexation gives فمك; فوك is not a restoration of a deleted mīm, but a form like ذو مال.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.anchor: فأما فم اسم رجل فإنك إذا أضفته قلت فمك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.claim: A man named ذو is annexed as ذواك, not ذوك, because ذو has no independent noun form when detached.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.anchor: لأنه لم يكن له اسم مفرد ولكن تقول ذواك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.claim: The adverbs لدى, إلى, and على change to لداك, إلاك, and علاك when they become personal names.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.anchor: إذا صرن أسماء لرجال أو لنساء قلت هذا لداك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.claim: Outside naming, لديك, عليك, and إليك preserve special forms that distinguish them from fully inflected nouns; proper names behave like ordinary nouns.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.anchor: كما فرقوا بين عني ومني وأخواتها وبين هني

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.claim: Al-Khalil reports that some Arabs say علاك, لداك, and إلاك, with the other genitive enclitic pronouns behaving like kāf.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.anchor: وحدثنا الخليل أن ناسا من العرب يقولون علاك ولداك وإلاك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.claim: كلا may take forms such as كليهما by analogy with عليك and لديك in oblique contexts, since both constructions are commonly annexed adverbs.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.anchor: وسألت الخليل عمن قال رأيت كلا أخويك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.claim: The analogy between كلا and على is based on frequent use and obligatory annexation; resemblance need not extend to every feature.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.anchor: لكثرتهما في كلامهم ولأنهما لا يخلوان من الإضافة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.claim: كلا is never singular; it always denotes a pair.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايتغيرفيالإضافةإلىالاسم.anchor: ولا تفرد كلا إنما تكون للمثنى أبدا

SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r1.claim: ونى يني ونيا means to slacken or grow weary, following the conjugation pattern وعد يعد وعدا.
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r1.anchor: يقال: ونى يني ونيا كوعد/ يعد وعدا إذا فترو

SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r2.claim: أناة describes a woman as slow in rising, figuratively indicating stoutness.
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r2.anchor: ومنه امرأة أناة، وصفوها بفتور القيام كناية عن ضخامتها

SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r3.claim: The original form was وناة, with hamza substituted for wāw as in أحد from وحد; the author says this is not regular analogy.
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r3.anchor: والأصل وناة. فأبدلوا الهمزة من الواو كأحد في وحد. وليس بالقياس

SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r4.claim: A hadith quotes God as loving two qualities in a person: clemency and deliberateness.
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث: " إن فيك لخصلتين يحبهما الله: الحلم والأناة "

SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r5.claim: الواني means one who falls short; an unnamed poet uses it in فما أنا بالواني ولا الضرع الغمر.
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r5.anchor: والواني: المقصر في أمره. قال الشاعر:

SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r7.claim: Some analyze ونى as a verb like زال and انفك, functioning like كان under negation or its equivalent, as in ما ونى زيد قائما (“he did not cease standing”).
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r7.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنه يكون من أخوات زال وانفك فيعمل بشرط النفي أو شبهه عمل كان

SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r8.speaker: ابن مالك
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r8.claim: Ibn Malik cites لا يني to mean “does not cease”; الحب with ḍamma means love and with kasra means the lover.
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r8.anchor: وأنشد الشيخ جمال الدين بن مالك شاهدا على ذلك قول الشاعر: 3291 لا يني الحب شيمة الحب ما دا

SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r9.claim: Those rejecting this syntax construe the poem with a dropped preposition because ونى can take عن or في; the author glosses it as love not slackening in a lover's character.
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r9.anchor: ومن منع ذلك يتأول البيت على حذف حرف الجر؛ فإن هذا الفعل يتعدى تارة ب عن وتارة ب في

SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r10.claim: In this verse the verb is construed with في, one of the prepositional complements used with ونى.
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r10.anchor: وقد عدي في الآية الكريمة ب في

SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r11.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r11.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads ولا تنيا with kasra on tāʾ by vowel assimilation; the yāʾ of ذكري is also quiescent.
SAMIN-DURR:20:42/r11.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب " ولا تنيا " بكسر التاء إتباعا لحركة النون

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p334/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p334/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p334/r6.claim: The question and answer glosses lā taniyā as 'do not grow weak in my command' and cites a poet's line using waniya for slackening.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p334/r6.anchor: قال: لا تضعفا عن أمري. وشاهده قول الشاعر: إني وجدك ما ونيت ولم أزل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p334/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p334/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p334/r7.claim: The form and root taniyā occur only here in the Qur'an, whereas weakness and its derivatives are frequent.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p334/r7.anchor: وحيدة في القرآن صيغة ومادة. وأما الضعف فكثير

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ opens the listed first-person yāʾs except ولي فيها and أخي اشدد, where he uses sukūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا اثنتين قوله ﴿ ولي فيها مآرب ﴾ وقوله ﴿ أخي اشدد ﴾ فإنه أسكنهما

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr uses sukūn on ولي فيها and حشرتني أعمى, opening the other listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.anchor: وأسكن أبو عمرو منها اثنتين / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ لم حشرتني أعمى ﴾ وفتح سائرها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr uses sukūn on ولي فيها، ويسر لي أمري، لذكري إن، على عيني إذ, and برأسي إني; he opens the rest.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.anchor: وأسكن ابن كثير منها خمسا / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ ويسر لي أمري ﴾ و ﴿ لذكري إن ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، ابن عامر، عاصم عن أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.claim: These readers use sukūn on all listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.anchor: وأسكنها كلها حمزة والكسائى وابن عامر وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر

NASHR:v2p171/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p171/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p171/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Abū Jaʿfar open the yāʾ in لنفسي اذهب and في ذكري اذهبا.
NASHR:v2p171/r2.anchor: وفتح نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر لنفسي اذهب، في ذكري اذهبا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p17#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p17#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p17#3/r1.claim: Qatada explains the command not to flag in remembrance as a command not to grow weak.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p17#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا تنيا في ذكري ﴾ قال لا تضعفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r1.claim: The gloss identifies الواني as one who slackens or weakens, matching the command not to grow weary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r1.anchor: فما أنا بالواني ولا الضرع الغمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r8.claim: وأخوك is coordinated with the implicit subject pronoun of فاذهب أنت; the same grammatical debate applies to فاذهب أنت وربك in al-Maida.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r8.anchor: وأخوك معطوف على الضمير المستكن في فاذهب أنت وربك في سورة المائدة وقول بعض النحاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r9.claim: Some grammarians instead parse وربك as nominative after an omitted verb, meaning “and let your Lord go”; the same question applies here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r9.anchor: أن وربك مرفوع على إضمار فعل، أي وليذهب ربك وذلك البحث جار هنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r10.claim: One report says God instructed Harun in Egypt to meet Moses; other accounts say he heard Moses was coming or was inspired to meet him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r10.anchor: وروي أن الله أوحى إلى هارون وهو بمصر أن يتلقى موسى. وقيل: سمع بمقدمه. وقيل: ألهم ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r11.claim: The plural may mean staff, hand, and tongue-knot, or the two signs of hand and staff; a plural can refer to a pair, as in another Qur’anic account.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r11.anchor: وظاهر بآياتي الجمع. فقيل: هي العصا، واليد، وعقدة لسانه. وقيل: اليد، والعصا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r12.claim: The staff itself contained multiple signs: it changed into an animal, grew from small to a serpent, and Moses could put his hand into its mouth unharmed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r12.anchor: وقيل العصا مشتملة على آيات انقلابها حيوانا، ثم في أول الأمر كانت صغيرة ثم عظمت حتى صارت ثعبانا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r13.claim: Another view understands the signs broadly as every miracle and revelation Moses was given.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r13.anchor: وقيل: ما أعطي من معجزة ووحي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r1.claim: The command to go with Aaron is a new sentence explaining what God’s special favor to Moses entails.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى ( اذهب انت واخوتك باياتى ( استئناف مسوق لبيان ما هو المقصود بالاصطناع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r2.claim: One parsing makes أخوك the subject of an understood “let your brother go,” in keeping with Moses’ request; another coordinates it with the implicit subject pronoun in اذهب, although a construction valid only as a dependent may not stand independently.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r2.anchor: أي وليذهب اخوك حسبما استدعيت وقيل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r3.claim: The signs are identified variously as the hand, staff, and speech knot; Ibn ʿAbbās says the nine signs, while another view says only the first two, with the plural commonly used for a pair.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r3.anchor: والايات المعجزات والمراد بها في قول اليد والعصا وحل العقدة وعن ابن عباس الآيات التسع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r4.claim: The view that the signs are the staff and hand is supported by Pharaoh’s request for a sign and Moses’ presentation of these two, which he calls “two proofs” (28:32).
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r4.anchor: قال له عليه السلام : فات با اية القى العصا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r5.claim: Some explain the plural even for two miracles because each contains several signs: the staff’s transformation, size, speed, submission, safety in its mouth, and return, and the hand’s whiteness, radiance, and restoration.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أنهما وان كانتا اثنتين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r6.claim: A broader view takes the signs as all Moses’ miracles and revelation, but al-Ālūsī favors the staff and hand: these alone are named as signs immediately before the command to go, and other signs such as resolving the speech knot are not called signs there (20:22).
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r6.anchor: واذي يميل اليه القلب أنه العصا واليد لما سمعت من المؤيد مع ما تقدم من أنه تعالى بعد ما أمره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r7.claim: The باء marks accompaniment, not transmission: Moses and Aaron go to Pharaoh equipped with and relying on the signs to fulfill the mission; this implies the signs were already present, while most of the nine had not yet occurred.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r7.anchor: ثم أن الباء للمصاحبة لا للتعدية إذ المراد ذهابهما إلى فرعون ملتبسين بالايات

ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r8.claim: The verb is from الوَنَى, “slackness,” and is normally intransitive; when made transitive it takes في or عن. Some Baghdadi grammarians instead treat it as a defective verb meaning زال, “continue,” an analysis Ibn Mālik chose; the lexicon explains لا يني يفعل as “keeps doing.”
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r8.anchor: من الونى بمعنى الفتور وهوفعل لازم وإذا عدى عدى بفى وبعن

ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r9.speaker: ابن وثاب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r9.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads the tāʾ with kasra by vowel assimilation to the following nūn; ʿAbd Allāh’s codex has لاتهنا, with the same sense of not flagging.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p193#3/r9.anchor: وقرا ابن وثاب ( ولاتنيا ) بكسر التاء اتباعه لحركة النون وفي مصحف عبد الله ( لاتهنا )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r1.claim: One explanation of “in My remembrance” is to remember God through the noble attributes and good acts befitting Him while conveying His message and calling people to worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r1.anchor: بما يليق بى من الصفات الجليلة والأفعال الجميلة عند تبليغ رسالتى والدعاء إلى عبادتى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r2.claim: A view transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās reads the command as “do not slack in conveying My message,” since remembrance can stand metaphorically for all worship and is its greatest form.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r2.anchor: وروى ذلك عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r3.claim: Another view means: do not forget God wherever you go; seek His help and support, knowing that nothing can be accomplished without remembering Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r3.anchor: لا تنسيانى حيثما تقلبتما واستمدا به العون

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r4.claim: Aaron is included in the dual prohibition even if he was absent at that moment, by the grammatical practice of giving precedence to the present addressee; this poses no difficulty.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194/r4.anchor: وجمع هرون مع موسى عليه السلام في صيغة نهى الحاضر بناء على القول بغيبته إذ ذاك للتغلب

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r1.claim: God’s signs here are Moses’ miracles.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r2.claim: The command means do not slacken or fall short.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r2.anchor: { ولا تنيا } ولا تفترا ولا تقصرا

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r3.speaker: قُرئ
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r3.claim: A reading uses kasra on the tāʾ.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r4.claim: They must remember God wherever they go and not forget Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r4.anchor: { فى ذكرى } لا تنسياني حيثما تقلبتما.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r5.claim: Alternatively, the command means to proclaim God’s remembrance and call people to Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:42/r5.anchor: وقيل في تبليغ ذكري والدعاء إلي.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p19/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p19/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p19/r21.claim: The renewed command repeats the earlier order, grants Moses the brother he requested, and sends them with the signs God showed him and further signs displayed through him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p19/r21.anchor: كما تقدم أمري لك به { اخوك } كما سألت { بلآيتي } التي أريتك وغيرها مما أظهره على يديك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p19/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p19/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p19/r22.claim: The prohibition means not to grow weak or slacken.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p19/r23.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p19/r23.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p19/r23.claim: Remembrance encompasses their whole mission, and they must pursue it intensely with full attention of heart because this best serves their purpose; Moses had made it the goal of his prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p19/r23.anchor: في غاية الاجتهاد فبه وإحضار القلب له , فإن ذلك أعون شيء على المراد

BURSEVI:v5p297/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p297/r1.claim: Dhahā means to go or depart and is used for both physical things and meanings, as in Abraham’s going to his Lord and the terror leaving Abraham.
BURSEVI:v5p297/r1.anchor: والذهاب المضي يقال ذهب بالشيء وأذهبه ويستعمل ذلك في الأعيان والمعاني

BURSEVI:v5p297/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p297/r2.claim: The instruction implies that Aaron too should go; he is coordinated in ellipsis because he was away from Moses at that time.
BURSEVI:v5p297/r2.anchor: أي : وليذهب أخوك هارون حسبما استدعيت عطف عليه

BURSEVI:v5p297/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p297/r3.claim: Brotherhood may be full, half, or by nursing, and is also figuratively used for people sharing a qibla, religion, craft, dealings, affection, or another affinity.
BURSEVI:v5p297/r3.anchor: ويستعار الأخ لكل مشارك لغيره في القبلة أو في الدين أو في صنعة أو في معاملة أو في مودة

BURSEVI:v5p297/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p297/r4.claim: My signs means God’s miracles; the preposition marks accompaniment, since Moses and Aaron go to Pharaoh equipped with the signs to carry out the prophetic mission, not merely to be delivered to him.
BURSEVI:v5p297/r4.anchor: بمعجزاتي والباء للمصاحبة لا للتعدية إذ المراد ذهابهما إلى فرعون ملتبسين بالآيات

BURSEVI:v5p297/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v5p297/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the signs as the nine sent down to Moses, even though some had not yet occurred.
BURSEVI:v5p297/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما يريد الآيات التسع التي أنزلت عليه وإن كان وقوع بعضها بالفعل مترقبا بعد

BURSEVI:v5p297/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p297/r6.claim: The plural may be honorific for the staff and hand, or may reflect al-Khalīl’s view that the minimum plural is two.
BURSEVI:v5p297/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الجمع للتعظيم والمراد العصا واليد

BURSEVI:v5p297/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p297/r7.claim: Taniyā means do not slack or flag; wany and its listed forms denote weakness or slackening.
BURSEVI:v5p297/r7.anchor: من ونى يني ونيا فهو وإن

BURSEVI:v5p297/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p297/r8.claim: They must persist in remembering God with tongue and heart in every state; remembrance enables every purpose, and neglect in other affairs results from neglect of God’s remembrance.

BURSEVI:v5p297/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p297/r9.claim: The reminder echoes Moses’ earlier prayer that the two might glorify and remember God much.
BURSEVI:v5p297/r9.anchor: وهو تذكير لقوله : {كى نسبحك كثيرا * ونذكرك كثيرا}

BURSEVI:v5p297/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297/r10.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p297/r10.claim: One explanation is that remembering God’s majesty makes all else seem small, so the soul grows strong and does not fear anyone else or weaken in its aim.
BURSEVI:v5p297/r10.anchor: قال بعضهم : الحكمة في هذا التكليف أن من ذكر جلال الله تعالى وعظمته

BURSEVI:v5p297/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297/r11.speaker: حضرة الهدايي
BURSEVI:v5p297/r11.claim: The Jelveti path’s master says beginning with divine oneness before exhortation makes listeners attentive and, by God’s help, makes the admonition effective.
BURSEVI:v5p297/r11.anchor: قال مرجع طريقتنا الجلوتية بالجيم حضرة الهدايى قدس سره التوحيد قبل الوعظ باعث لإصغاء السامعين

BURSEVI:v5p297/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297/r12.speaker: العرائس
BURSEVI:v5p297/r12.claim: Al-ʿArāʾis reads the command as a warning not to become absent from divine witnessing while occupied with God’s work, lest one be fatigued away from God by serving Him.
BURSEVI:v5p297/r12.anchor: وفي "العرائس" : لا تغيبا عن مشاهدتي باشتغالكما بأمري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r1.claim: Sharing the mission with Aaron multiplies the call and also spurs Aaron to preach; their messages glorify God, teach His attributes and commandments, and bring the people into faith and piety, multiplying remembrance through proclamation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r1.anchor: تشريكه في الدعوة ولم يكن لأخيه من قبل ، وذلك يجعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr connects the benefits Moses requested with the command not to slacken in remembrance: delivering God's commands and prohibitions increases their glorification and remembrance.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r3.claim: Cooperation in the mission lets the brothers divide the work needed for daily life, reducing time spent on necessities and freeing more time for preaching.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r3.anchor: تقليل من الاشتغال بضرورات الحياة ، إذ يمكن أن يقتسما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r4.claim: Moses knew Pharaoh's severity and tyranny would obstruct the people from leaving misguidance, and that preaching would expose its callers to trial; he sought help to overcome that trial and devote themselves to remembrance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p213/r4.anchor: علمه بشدة فرعون وطغيانه ومنعه الأمة من مفارقة ضلالهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r1.claim: The preferred view takes ‘My signs’ as the staff and the hand, although dual signs can be expressed with a plural.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r1.anchor: أحدها أنها العصا واليد وقد يذكر الاثنان بلفظ الجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari's second view includes the staff, the hand, and the undoing of the knot known to Pharaoh and his people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r2.anchor: والثاني العصا واليد وحل العقدة التي ما زال فرعون وقومه يعرفونها ذكره ابن الأنباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r3.claim: A third view identifies the signs as the nine signs given to Moses.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba says lā taniyā means do not grow weak or slack; wani ya-ni is another form of the verb.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة لا تضعفا ولا تفترا يقال ونى يني في الأمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r5.claim: One explanation takes the remembrance as the mission to Pharaoh.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r5.anchor: وفي المراد بالذكر هاهنا قولان أحدهما أنه الرسالة إلى فرعون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r6.claim: The other explanation takes the remembrance as carrying out the religious duties, glorifying God, and proclaiming His oneness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p286#3/r6.anchor: والثاني أنه القيام بالفرائض والتسبيح والتهليل

MUJAHID:v1p397/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p397/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p397/r1.claim: Do not grow weak or flag in remembering God.
MUJAHID:v1p397/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ولا تنيا في ذكري ﴾ يقول لا تضعفا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p55#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p55#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p55#3/r2.claim: Do not grow slack: wanā means weakness and falling short.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p55#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ ولا تنيا ﴾ تفترا من الوني وهو الفتور والتقصير

NASAFI-FULL:v3p55#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p55#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p55#3/r3.claim: God's remembrance may be the wing on which they fly, or may mean conveying the message, the greatest of the acts of worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p55#3/r3.anchor: أي اتخذا ذكري جناحا تطيران به أو أريد بالذكر تبليغ الرسالة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies God's signs as the nine signs sent to Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد التسع الآيات التي أنزلت عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as do not grow weak in the mission; Qatāda agrees.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تضعفا أي في أمر الرسالة وقاله قتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r6.claim: Others explain it as do not slacken; the cited verse about Muḥammad attests the sense of not flagging.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r6.anchor: وقيل: تفترا. قال الشاعر: فما ونى محمد مذ ان غفر

QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r7.claim: The root conveys weakness, languor, weariness, and fatigue, all relevant to the command.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r7.anchor: والونى الضعف والفتور، والكلال والإعياء وكله مراد في الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r8.speaker: امرؤ القيس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r8.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses الونى for weariness in his description of racing horses.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r8.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس: مسح إذا ما السابحات على الونى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r9.speaker: أبان
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r9.claim: Abān understands the phrase as do not cease; Ṭarafa's cauldrons that never stop boiling illustrate the usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r9.anchor: وبه فسر أبان معنى الآية واستشهد بقول طرفة: كأن القدور الراسيات أمامهم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also explains it as do not be slow.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا: لا تبطئا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads ولا تهنا and glosses remembrance as praise, glorification, and conveying God's message.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:41-42/r11.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود «ولا تهنا في ذكري» وتحميدي وتمجيدي وتبليغ رسالتي.

STUDYQURAN:20:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:42/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:42/r1.claim: God's signs here are the nine signs given to Moses.
STUDYQURAN:20:42/r1.anchor: My signs refers to the nine signs given to Moses

STUDYQURAN:20:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:42/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:42/r2.claim: Not tiring in God's remembrance means not weakening in conveying the message.
STUDYQURAN:20:42/r2.anchor: Tire not in the remembrance of Me means to not weaken in conveying the message

STUDYQURAN:20:42/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:42/r3.speaker: spiritual interpretation
STUDYQURAN:20:42/r3.claim: A spiritual reading warns against invoking God with the tongue while the heart remains inattentive to the One invoked.
STUDYQURAN:20:42/r3.anchor: According to a spiritual interpretation of this verse, it means that one should not invoke God only with the tongue

TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r2.claim: Moses is to go with Aaron to Pharaoh carrying God's proofs and deliver His messages because Pharaoh has rebelled in error.
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r2.anchor: هارون {بآياتي} [البقرة: 41] يقول: بأدلتي وحججي، اذهبا إلى فرعون بها إنه تمرد في ضلاله وغيه، فأبلغاه رسالاتي

TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r3.claim: They must not weaken in remembering God; remembrance strengthens resolve and steadies them by recalling His countless blessings.
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r3.anchor: ولا تضعفا في أن تذكراني فيما أمرتكما ونهيتكما، فإن ذكركما إياي يقوي عزائمكما، ويثبت أقدامكما

TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r4.claim: Wanā means to weaken; al-ʿAjjāj's verse about Muhammad not weakening is cited as evidence.
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r4.anchor: يقال منه: ونى فلان في هذا الأمر، وعن هذا الأمر: إذا ضعف، وهو يني ونيا كما قال العجاج

TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as do not delay.
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r5.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولا تنيا} [طه: 42] يقول: لا تبطئا

TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also says not to weaken in remembering God.
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله {ولا تنيا في ذكري} [طه: 42] يقول: ولا تضعفا في ذكري

TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid glosses the command as do not weaken.
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ولا تنيا في ذكري} [طه: 42] قال: لا تضعفا

TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r8.claim: Qatāda says not to weaken in remembering God.
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولا تنيا في ذكري} [طه: 42] يقول: لا تضعفا في ذكري

TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r9.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk likewise says not to weaken.
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r9.anchor: الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {ولا تنيا في ذكري} [طه: 42] يقول: لا تضعفا

TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd explains al-wānī as inattentive and negligent.
TAB-FULL:v16p72#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ولا تنيا في ذكري} [طه: 42] قال: الواني: هو الغافل المفرط

SULAMI:v1p445#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p445#2/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p445#2/r1.claim: Sahl warns against abundant verbal remembrance that leaves the heart inattentive and unwatchful.
SULAMI:v1p445#2/r1.anchor: قال سهل : لا تكثر الذكر باللسان

TUSTARI:20:42/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:20:42/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:20:42/r1.claim: The command means not to tire the tongue with abundant remembrance while neglecting the heart's watchfulness.
TUSTARI:20:42/r1.anchor: أي لا تكثر الذكر باللسان، وتغفل عن مراقبة القلب

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#2/r1.claim: Taniyā means do not weaken or slacken; its verbal forms include waniya yanī and wani yunā.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#2/r1.anchor: ولا تنيا} أي لا تضعفا ولا تفترا. يقال: ونى في الأمر يني.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the signs as the nine signs with which Moses was sent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يعني الآيات التسع التي بعث بها موسى)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r2.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r2.claim: Others understand the signs as God’s proofs.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the signs may mean the staff and hand, with a plural used for two, or those signs together with the resolution of Moses’ speech impediment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: (يجوز أن يريد {بآياتي} العصا، واليد، وأوقع عليهما اسم الجمع، ويجوز أن يريدهما مع حل العقدة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi reports that Aaron was in Egypt and was inspired to meet Moses; when they met, Moses told him God had commanded him to go to Pharaoh and that he had asked God to send Aaron with him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي: (وكان هارون يومئذ بمصر، فألهم أن يتلقى موسى، فتلقاه من مصر، فلما لقي موسى قال له موسى: إن الله أمرني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r5.claim: The commentators gloss the command as “do not weaken or slacken.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ولا تنيا} أي: (لا تضعفا ولا تفترا)، قاله المفسرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r6.claim: The verb wanā means to weaken; the author cites the related forms and a line by al-ʿAjjaj using the root for the Prophet’s constancy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p407/r6.anchor: يقال: ونى، يني، ونيا، ووان إذا ضعف (¬1). قال العجاج (¬2):

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408/r1.claim: Al-Farra says “in My remembrance” and “from My remembrance” are equivalent; the command is not to neglect remembrance through gratitude for God’s kindness and favor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: (في ذكري، وعن ذكري سواء) (¬3). والمعنى: لا تقصرا في ذكري بالإحسان إليكما

TABATABAI:20:41-44/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r7.claim: The command renews the earlier order to Moses alone, adding Aaron because Moses asked that his brother share the mission; both are now addressed.
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r7.anchor: تجديد للأمر السابق خطابا لموسى وحده في قوله { إذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى }

TABATABAI:20:41-44/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r8.claim: Although only two signs had yet been given, the plural promises Moses further divine support when other signs are needed.
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r8.anchor: ولم يؤت وقتئذ إلا آيتين وعد جميل بأنه مؤيد بغيرهما

TABATABAI:20:41-44/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r9.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r9.claim: The author rejects the claim that the plural simply denotes the two signs, or that each sign unfolds into many signs.
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r9.anchor: وأما القول بأن المراد هما الآيتان والجمع ربما يطلق على الإثنين،

TABATABAI:20:41-44/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r10.claim: “Do not be slack” prohibits languor; in context, remembrance means calling people to belief in God alone, not inward or verbal recollection.
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r10.anchor: نهي عن الوني وهو الفتور، والأنسب للسياق السابق أن يكون المراد بالذكر الدعوة إلى الإيمان

TABRISI:20:40-44/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:40-44/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:40-44/r12.claim: God's signs here mean His proofs and evidences.

TABRISI:20:40-44/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:40-44/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:40-44/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the signs to mean the nine miracles.

TABRISI:20:40-44/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:40-44/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:40-44/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas reads this as not weakening in God's mission.
TABRISI:20:40-44/r14.anchor: أي ولا تضعفا في رسالتي عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:20:40-44/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:40-44/r15.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:20:40-44/r15.claim: Al-Suddi reads it as not slackening in God's command.
TABRISI:20:40-44/r15.anchor: وقيل: ولا تفترا في أمري عن السدي

TABRISI:20:40-44/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:40-44/r16.speaker: محمد بن كعب
TABRISI:20:40-44/r16.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says not to fall short in God's command because fear of Pharaoh might make them slacken.
TABRISI:20:40-44/r16.anchor: ولا تقصرا عن محمد بن كعب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:41-43/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:41-43/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:41-43/r2.claim: The signs are the miracles God gave Moses and Aaron.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:41-43/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:41-43/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:41-43/r3.claim: Moses and Aaron are told not to grow slack.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r1.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r1.claim: Mujāhid glosses this as do not weaken in remembering Me.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r1.anchor: المعلى، عن أبي يحيى، عن مجاهد قال: ولا تضعفا في ذكري.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r2.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r2.claim: Al-Hasan takes it as calling people to God and conveying His message.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: في الدعاء إلي والتبليغ عني رسالتي.

ITQAN:v2p350/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p350/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p350/r1.claim: La taniya means do not weaken in carrying out My command; an anonymous poetic line uses waniytu to attest this sense.
ITQAN:v2p350/r1.anchor: قال لا تضعفا عن أمري قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك قال نعم أما سمعت قول الشاعر

ITQAN:v2p320/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p320/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p320/r5.claim: “Do not slacken” means “do not be slow.”

DAMGHANI:v1p182/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p182/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p182/r9.claim: Dhikr can mean affirmation of God's oneness; the source groups this with a parallel in Sūrat al-Zukhruf.
DAMGHANI:v1p182/r9.anchor: " ومن أعرض عن ذكري " يعني توحيدي نظيره في سورة الزخرف

ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r3.claim: Waniyā means do not weaken or slacken; the verb waniya and the expression tawānā describe becoming lax and weak.
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r3.anchor: معناه ولا تضعفا، يقال: ونى يني ونيا

NASHR:v2p322/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r5.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p322/r5.claim: For five yāʾs of annexation—إني آنست, إني أنا ربك, إنني أنا الله, لنفسي اذهب, and في ذكري—the two Medinese, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read the yāʾ open.
NASHR:v2p322/r5.anchor: إني آنست، إني أنا ربك، إنني أنا الله، لنفسي اذهب، في ذكري اذهبا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r3.claim: God's signs are His proofs and evidences.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the signs as the nine signs with which Moses was sent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يعني الآيات التسع التي بعث بها موسى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r5.claim: The command means do not weaken.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r5.anchor: ولا تنيا} لا تضعفا، وقال السدي: لا تفترا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r6.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r6.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the command as do not slacken.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b glosses the command as do not fall short.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r7.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: لا تقصرا {في ذكري}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو وأهل الحجاز
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r8.claim: Abu Amr and the people of the Hijaz read the yāʾ with fatḥa in li-nafsī and dhikrī and in the cited forms at 25:30 and 61:6; Abu Bakr agrees on the latter form, while the rest use sukūn.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r8.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو، وأهل الحجاز: "لنفسي اذهب"، "وذكري اذهبا"، و"إن قومي اتخذوا"

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r2.claim: Aaron was absent when God first spoke to Moses, so the command anticipates their later meeting in Egypt and instructs Moses to tell him to accompany him; it is not immediate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r2.anchor: لأن هارون لم يكن حاضرا حين كلم الله موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r3.claim: The باء marks accompaniment: Moses is reassured that God's signs, proofs of his truth before Pharaoh, will accompany him.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r4.claim: ولا تنيا means do not weaken or slacken in the work; Moses is directly forbidden, and is to tell Aaron the same, with the prohibition used literally and figuratively.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r1.claim: God sends Moses and Aaron to invite Pharaoh; He addresses Moses alone as an honor, though Aaron may also have received revelation through an angel to go.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r1.anchor: أمر الله تعالى موسى وهارون في هذه الآية بالنفوذ إلى دعوة فرعون وخاطب موسى وحده تشريفا له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r2.claim: God's signs include the miracles and signs given to the two, as well as revelation, commands, and prohibitions such as the Torah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r2.anchor: وبآياتي معناه بعلاماتي التي أعطيتكموها من معجزة وآية ووحي وأمر ونهي كالتوراة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r3.claim: ولا تنيا means do not weaken or delay; ونى describes slackening through weakness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r3.anchor: وتنيا معناه تضعفا وتبطيا تقول ونا فلان في أمر كذا إذا تباطأ فيه عن ضعف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r4.claim: الونى means fatigue, slackness, or failure in people and animals, as illustrated by a line of verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r4.anchor: والونى الكلال والفتور والفشل في البهائم والإنس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud's codex reads ولا تهنا في ذكري, meaning do not become soft or yielding.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r5.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود «ولا تهنا في ذكري» معناه ولا تلينا من قولك هين لين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r1.claim: God's signs here mean His proofs, demonstrations, and miracles.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r2.speaker: علي ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ali ibn Abi Talha, glosses the command as: do not delay.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r2.anchor: قال علي ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس: لا تبطئا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r3.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r3.claim: Mujahid, reporting from Ibn Abbas, glosses it as: do not weaken.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد، عن ابن عباس: لا تضعفا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r4.claim: Moses and Aaron must persist in remembering God while facing Pharaoh; remembrance strengthens them and overcomes him, as a hadith describes the servant who remembers God while confronting his opponent.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r4.anchor: والمراد أنهما لا يفتران في ذكر الله، بل يذكران الله في حال مواجهة فرعون

JISHUMI:v7p4666/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r6.claim: The common reading is lā taniyā; Ibn Masud's reported lā tahinā means do not weaken, but the author says only the widely transmitted reading is valid.
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r6.anchor: قراءة العامة: (لا تنيا)، وعن ابن مسعود: (لا تهنا) بمعنى لا تضعفا

JISHUMI:v7p4666/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r8.claim: Wanā, with either vowel on the first syllable, means slackness or weakness in an undertaking; al-wanā can also mean fatigue, and awnaytu means I tired someone.
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r8.anchor: الونى والونى بفتح الواو وضمها: الفتور في الأمر والضعف، ووني في الأمر يني ونيا

JISHUMI:v7p4666/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r9.speaker: العجاج
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r9.claim: Al-Ajjaj's verse uses wanā for slackening: Muhammad did not flag after God forgave him.
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r9.anchor: قال العجاج: فما ونى محمد مذ أن غفر ... له الإله ما مضى وما غبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r1.claim: Al-wanā is slackness or shortcoming; one reading has the prefix vowel assimilated, yielding “do not slacken in remembering Me.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r1.anchor: الونى . الفتور والتقصير . وقرىء ( تنيا ) بكسر حرف المضارعة للإتباع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r2.claim: The command means not to forget God; He remains in their remembrance wherever they go, and His remembrance is their source of aid and support, since affairs succeed through it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r2.anchor: أي : لا تنسياني ولا أزال منكما على ذكر حيثما تقلبتما ، واتخذا ذكري جناحا تصيران به مستمدين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r3.claim: “Remembrance” may also mean conveying the message: dhikr covers worship generally, and conveying the message is among its greatest forms.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد بالذكر تبليغ الرسالة ، فإن الذكر يقع على سائر العبادات ، وتبليغ الرسالة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r4.claim: One report says God revealed to Aaron, while he was in Egypt, that he should meet Moses.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r4.anchor: روي : أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى هارون وهو بمصر أن يتلقى موسى .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r5.claim: Another account says Aaron heard that Moses was approaching.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r6.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r6.claim: A further account says Aaron was inspired to meet Moses.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r5.claim: One interpretation is “do not slacken in remembering Me”; the cited line about Muhammad's steadfastness illustrates ونى.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r5.anchor: لا تفترا في ذكري , قال الشاعر : فما ونى محمد مذ أن غفر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r6.claim: Qatada interprets the command as “do not grow weak in My mission.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r6.anchor: لا تضعفا في رسالتي , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets the command as “do not delay.”

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r8.speaker: أبان
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r8.claim: Aban interprets it as “do not cease” and cites a line by Ṭarafa describing pots that never stop boiling.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r8.anchor: لا تزالا , حكاه أبان واستشهد بقول طرفة : كأن القدور الراسيات أمامهم

MUQATIL:20:41-45/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r2.claim: The signs are the hand and staff; Aaron was in Egypt, and the brothers met before reaching Pharaoh.

MUQATIL:20:41-45/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r3.claim: They must not weaken in God's cause or in delivering the message to Pharaoh, which emboldens them to face him.
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r3.anchor: يقول: ولا تضعفا فى أمرى، فى قراءة ابن مسعود

MUQATIL:20:41-45/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r4.claim: Ibn Masud reads the phrase as do not weaken in My remembrance in delivering to Pharaoh.
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r4.anchor: فى قراءة ابن مسعود: " ولا تهنا فى ذكرى

BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r3.claim: Bursevī postpones explaining why another verse uses the plural “My signs” until its later discussion.
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r3.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى : {اذهب أنت وأخوك بااياتى} (طه : 42)

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r1.claim: Rāzī reads the bāʾ as “with”: without a sign Moses and Aaron could not obligate Pharaoh to believe, showing the error of blind imitation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r1.anchor: الباء ههنا بمعنى مع وذلك لأنهما لو ذهبا إليه بدون آية معهما لم يلزمه الإيمان وذلك من أقوى الدلائل على فساد التقليد

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r2.claim: The first reported view identifies the signs as Moses’ staff and hand, since these are the signs named in this and other accounts before Pharaoh asks for another sign.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r2.anchor: أحدها : أنها اليد والعصا لأنهما اللذان جرى ذكرهما في هذا الموضع وفي سائر المواضع

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r3.speaker: أصحاب القول الأول
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r3.claim: They defend the plural by counting the staff’s transformations and harmlessness, and the hand’s whiteness, radiance, and disappearance, as multiple signs.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r3.anchor: أجابوا بوجوه : الأول : أن العصا ما كانت آية واحدة بل كانت آيات

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r4.speaker: أصحاب القول الأول
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r4.claim: Even one staff gives several proofs: God’s power, knowledge and wisdom, Moses’ prophethood, and resurrection, so the two signs contain many signs.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r4.anchor: لكن فيها آيات كثيرة لأن انقلابها حية يدل على وجود إله قادر على الكل عالم بالكل حكيم ويدل على نبوة موسى

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r5.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r5.claim: A further answer is that Arabic usage can treat two items as the minimum plural.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r5.anchor: من الناس من قال : أقل الجمع إثنان على ما عرفت في أصول الفقه

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r6.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r6.claim: The second view takes the command to mean God will furnish them with whatever signs are needed to remove Pharaoh’s and his people’s excuses.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r6.anchor: القول الثاني : أن قوله : { اذهبا * بآياتي } معناه أني أمدكما بآياتي وأظهر على أيديكما من الآيات ما تزاح به العلل

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r7.claim: The third view counts three miracles: the staff, the hand, and Moses’ resolution of the knot in his speech.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r7.anchor: القول الثالث : أن الله تعالى آتاه العصا واليد وحل عقدة لسانه وذلك أيضا معجز فكانت الآيات ثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r8.claim: The word wanī means slackness, languor, or falling short.

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r9.claim: A reading has the imperfect prefix vowel kasra, by assimilation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r9.anchor: وقرىء ولا تنيا بكسر حرف المضارعة للاتباع

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r10.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r10.claim: One interpretation makes remembrance a means of accomplishing aims: awareness of God’s majesty makes others seem insignificant, strengthens resolve, and gratitude sustains obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r10.anchor: المعنى لا تنيا بل اتخذا ذكرى آلة لتحصيل المقاصد واعتقدا أن أمرا من الأمور لا يتمشى لأحد إلا بذكري

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r11.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r11.claim: Another takes remembrance as conveying the message, the greatest form of worship.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r11.anchor: المراد بالذكر تبليغ الرسالة فإن الذكر يقع على كل العبادات وتبليغ الرسالة من أعظمها

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r12.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r12.claim: A third means they should remind Pharaoh and his people that God rejects unbelief and warn them with reward and punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r12.anchor: قوله : { ولا تنيا فى ذكرى } عند فرعون وكيفية الذكر هو أن يذكرا لفرعون وقومه أن الله تعالى لا يرضى

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r13.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r13.claim: A fourth interpretation is to recount God’s favors and kindnesses to Pharaoh.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r13.anchor: أن يذكرا لفرعون آلاء الله ونعماءه وأنواع إحسانه إليه
